rv.q: Getting an insightful exploration of how two actors saved Shakespeare’s legacy for all time is an extraordinary treat for theater buffs and a special gift for lovers of Shakespeare.
This exquisite play is a love letter to the genius and legacy of William Shakespeare, arguably the greatest English language playwright.
After you see Promethean Theatre ’s excellent production of The Book of Will , consider what the world of theater would be like if the King’s Men had not succeeded in their quest.
You certainly don't have to be a fan to fall in love with this sweet, unhurried play.
It is that premise that makes the play richer and more affecting than it has any right to be.

Promethean’s The Book of Will is playing for three more weekends at the Den Theatre and is a truly enjoyable night at the theatre, reminding us all that great work can take a village, and, of course, that where there’s a Will, there’s a way.
By focusing on the heart and wit of Shakespeare over the nitty-gritty history, Gunderson's The Book of Will succeeds at making the populist case for his work.
Nevertheless, “The Book of Will” tells an important story of the epic accomplishment of two devotees of Shakespeare, and one well worth hearing and seeing.
It is a much-needed, fun night out at the theatre.

The point that Gunderson makes us see quite clearly, in dialogue and thematically, is how great literature can be brought to life, how it can enrich all of our lives, how it can ring in the ears and stir the emotions.
If you’re in the mood for a mostly true show about how we have many of Shakespeare’s works that’s cute and funny, The Book of Will would be a good fit for you.

cn.t: Critics praise Lauren Gunderson's heartfelt and humorous dramatization of Shakespeare's First Folio creation, celebrating its blend of historical fact with emotional storytelling and unexpected comedy that brings the Bard's legacy vividly to life.
